messages:
incidents-bot: [ALERT] hosted-us-east-1: GPU pool "hosted-gpu-pool-1" saturated; request queue depth > 4800; p95 latency spiked from 240ms -> 3.1s. Auto-scaler failing to create new nodes (quota errors).

Ava (oncall): I'm seeing the spike in the hosted API dashboards. P95/99 for /v1/generate jumping. Backlog is growing in the host-queue service. Starting investigation.

Ava (oncall): prometheus query: sum(rate(hosted_queue_depth[1m])) = 4821; provisioner_create_errors{reason="QUOTA_EXCEEDED"} spiking in logs.

Maya (infra-engineer): digging into provisioner logs now. Getting 403 from cloud API: "QuotaExceeded: GPU quota reached in us-east-1". Provisioner attempted 8 creations in last 2m and all failed.

Ava (oncall): Customer-facing impact — several high-volume tenants reporting 504s and retries. Priya, any CCs / escalations?

Priya (cs): We have 3 customers (tenant-831, tenant-992, tenant-44) on support channel complaining about timeouts for generation requests. CS triage on it — adding status page note pending mitigation.

Ava (oncall): Short-term mitigation plan: 1) Enable traffic shedding for non-enterprise tiers (rate-limit to 5r/s) 2) Route requests to CPU fallback pool for small models 3) Enable canary fallback to quantized model variant to reduce GPU load.

Maya (infra-engineer): Applied rate-limit rule to route 60% of burst traffic to cpu-fallback (small models). Provisioner still shows quota errors; infra is requesting quota increase but that won't be immediate.

Ava (oncall): ops-bot, runbook link and commands? paste

ops-bot: Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/hosted-gpu-saturation

ops-bot: Helpful commands:
`````
# view recent prov errors
kubectl logs deploy/provisioner -n infra --since=10m | grep QUOTA_EXCEEDED
# add temporary rate-limit rule
redwoodctl policies create rate-limit --scope non-enterprise --limit 5r/s
`````

Diego (next-oncall): I'm oncall in 30m. Ava, anything I should prioritize during handoff?

Ava (oncall): Handoff notes for Diego: - Current status: GPU pool saturated; autoscaler failing with quota errors. - Temporary mitigations applied: non-enterprise rate-limit, 60% traffic routed to cpu-fallback, canary quantized variant enabled for small models. - Customer impact: 3 tenants hitting 504s; overall error rate still elevated ~6% - What we need: 1) Monitor queue depth and p95/p99; 2) When quota increase is live, validate provisioner can create nodes and drain cpu-fallback; 3) If quota update delayed, consider proactive throttles or rolling restarts of heavy model instances.

Maya (infra-engineer): Cloud quota request submitted (case #CLD-4892). Support said ETA ~2h. We'll try to stagger node creation to not hit the quota bucket. Also looking at freeing up unused preemptible pools.

Ava (oncall): Priya — please update customers with temporary mitigations and expected ETA ~2h; offer credits for failed requests. Mark incident severity P1 -> currently P1 due to real customer impact.

Priya (cs): Doing customer update now. Will post status page and DM account leads.

Ava (oncall): Monitoring: p95 baseline dropping slightly after rate-limit, but p99 still high for heavy prompts. Queue depth 1m avg now 2.1k (down from 4.8k). Keep an eye on request throttles and errors.

Diego (next-oncall): On handoff — will keep the run for 2h and coordinate with Maya on quota. If no quota lift, plan is to scale down max-concurrency for large models and force more routing to quantized variants. I'll update here at next checkpoint (in 30m).

Ava (oncall): Thanks. Leaving handoff: summary pinned. Logging this thread to incidents channel and incident manager. If anyone else sees a new customer report drop into #support, flag it.

incidents-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0589. Assigned owners: Ava (primary), Diego (secondary), Maya (infra). SEV: P1. Runbook attached.

Diego (next-oncall): Checkpoint (30m): queue depth 1m avg 1.5k; p95 780ms; p99 3.5s for large models. Cloud quota still pending. No new customer escalation in last 15m. Proceeding to reduce concurrency for model-x-large from 8->4.

Maya (infra-engineer): Applied concurrency cap for model-x-large. Provisioner creation rate capped to 1 creation per 30s to avoid immediate quota bucket refill.

Ava (oncall): Noting mitigation: concurrency cap + canary quantized variant moved ~25% of traffic off GPUs. Keep monitoring.

Priya (cs): Updated tenants with current mitigations and expected ETA for quota. One tenant asked for formal RCA — will coordinate post-incident.

Diego (next-oncall): Leaving note: if quota case resolves, let's validate with a single node create test then gradually ramp. If still stuck after 2h, consider emergency failover to dedicated reserved cloud pool for affected tenants (requires config change and billing approval).

Ava (oncall): Acknowledged. I'll stay until quota resolves. Marking last update here; if no further changes, we'll update incident timeline and move to postmortem.

incidents-bot: Incident status updated: mitigation in place. Next update scheduled in 60m.
